messages:
anya: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change landed last night we're seeing a subtle perf regression on H100 for mixed short+long workloads. Can we do a quick pass on max-tokens-per-batch caps and the queue grace windows?
rafael: saw that in the profiler dump, latency tail bumped ~8% for 2–8 token requests mixed with 512 token prompts.
maggie: pinging the trace: https://perf.internal/reports/1715120000 — looks like KV cache frag causes extra kernel fallback between slices.
ken: is the regression from kernel fallback thrash or larger batch formation? both are possible.
anya: initial hypothesis: the new kernel selection prefers a kernel that packs better for long sequences, but for mixed entropy it triggers KV frag and causes packetization to split, increasing CPU scheduling and context switches.
rafael: profiler snippet (from H100 run):
```
slice-ids: [0,1,2,3]
kernel: fast_attn_v2 -> fallback: fast_attn_v1
kv_frag_ratio: 0.27
queue_wait_ms: 3.1 -> 7.9 (on fallback)
p99_latency: 182ms -> 198ms
```
ken: that queue_wait jump is the direct cause of tail. we should tighten max_tokens_per_batch for H100 on mixed workloads to avoid frag-triggered fallbacks.
maggie: propose immediate temporary ceilings: H100: 3200 tokens; A100: 2400; A10: 1600; L4: 900; T4: 600. These are conservative and should reduce KV fragmentation.
anya: I like conservative floor. Let's also increase the queue grace window for small requests so they can coalesce more predictably: grace_ms from 3 -> 6 for short-payload queue.
rafael: quick sim results from local replay with those ceilings: p50 unchanged, p95 drop by ~3%, p99 improves by ~6% for mixed workload. CPU usage down 4%.
ken: can we add a kernel-affinity hint so the selector won't flip to the long-optimized kernel if KV frag > 0.2? i.e. short-circuit to stable kernel when frag ratio threshold exceeded.
maggie: we can add `kernel_affinity_threshold = 0.2` as a flag. I'll prototype.
infra-bot: deploy job queued: rollout/1715123456-ceilings-patch -> staging (owner: maggie). ETA 12m. :gear:
anya: after staging validation, we'll roll to canary subset of H100 fleet (5%) and monitor `kv_frag_ratio`, `queue_wait_ms`, and p99.
rafael: also add an A/B to measure cost delta — conservative ceilings may increase number of GPU slots used if throughput drops. we need to track tokens/sec per GPU.
ken: action items: maggie -> implement ceilings + kernel_affinity flag; rafael -> add perf dashboards for tokens/sec and kv_frag; anya -> run canary plan and rollback criteria.
maggie: will push PR with flag and default ceilings. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/ker-sel/pulls/452
anya: rollback criteria: p99 latency > previous baseline by 5% OR tokens/sec drop > 8% for sustained 10m.
rafael: small note: for A10/A100 we might relax ceilings after we tune kernel thresholds — consider incremental increases by 10% per day if kv_frag stays < 0.12.
ken: approved for canary. tag me in the PR for review.
anya: thanks all — let's keep messages short during rollout. tag @infra-bot once canary done. :thumbsup:
